notable_absence.finding: The page states: 'Note that both role and user must already exist. Nonexistent roles don't cause an error, but have no effect on the user's access privileges.' This is a fail-silent behavior for a malformed/typo'd role assignment - assigning a user to a role that doesn't exist is accepted without complaint and simply grants nothing. This is a materially different failure mode from server/'s RBAC (which, per the prior batch, errors on invalid privilege/role names) and worth flagging as a docs/product behavior contrast rather than a documentation gap per se.

cross_product_finding: Role assignment in SGW has three interchangeable mechanisms (Admin REST API admin_roles field, Sync Function role() call, legacy config admin_roles field) that all reduce to the same underlying assignsRole relationship - there is no single canonical grant path the way Capella's console/API-key-scoped role assignment is comparatively centralized, nor a single privilege-grant statement the way server/'s GRANT ROLE works. The role() sync-function path is the most novel: it lets assignment happen as a SIDE EFFECT of document processing (a document's content or XATTR can cause a user to be assigned a role while that document is being synced), meaning role membership in SGW can be driven by application data flowing through the system rather than only by an administrator's explicit out-of-band grant action - a shape with no parallel in either server/'s or Capella's static grant models.
